title: Time to Rebuild Kashmir’s Apex Chamber

ai.summary: The article discusses the need for business associations in Jammu and Kashmir to unite for environmental and economic issues, highlighting the role of the Nigeen Tourist Traders Association and environmental initiatives. It suggests forming a unified apex chamber to address collective concerns.

facts.claim: Kashmir has no shortage of business associations, trade bodies or organisations claiming to represent civil society. Their numbers have multiplied over the decades, each speaking for a particular trade, profession, locality or economic activity.
facts.quote: Kashmir has no shortage of business associations, trade bodies or organisations claiming to represent civil society. Their numbers have multiplied over the decades, each speaking for a particular trade, profession, locality or economic activity.

facts.claim: Both organisations are headed by businessman and environmental campaigner Manzoor Ahmad Wangnoo, whose dedication, alongside his committed team, to restoring water bodies, promoting plantation and mobilising public participation deserves recognition.

facts.claim: Governments may legislate and regulate, but society must actively participate in protecting the environment.

facts.claim: When Maharaja Hari Singh’s rule ended in 1947, we inherited a Jammu and Kashmir endowed with extraordinary biodiversity, magnificent forests, pristine lakes, rivers and wetlands.

facts.claim: The Federation of Chambers of Industries Kashmir (FCIK) brings together industrial estate, district and sector-based associations, enabling collective participation in industrial policy formulation.
